Maynard FM Jr et al. developed international standards for the neurological and functional classification of spinal cord injuries, as outlined by the American Spinal Injury Association in the journal Spinal Cord in 1997. 5. Guidelines for the management of acute cervical spinal injuries were published in the journal Neurosurgery in 2002, providing a detailed framework for clinical care. 6. Mann R and Heimbach D discussed the prognosis and treatment of burns in the Western Journal of Medicine in 1996, offering insights into effective management strategies. 7. Mock CN, Ofosu A, and Gish O investigated the use of district health services by injured individuals in rural Ghana, with findings published in the International Journal of Health Planning and Management in 2001. 9. The World Health Organization (WHO) published a manual in 1996 aimed at promoting independence following spinal cord injuries, specifically designed for mid-level rehabilitation workers. 10. The WHO released the 12th Model List of Essential Medicines in April 2002, providing a comprehensive guide to essential pharmaceuticals. 11. Reich MR explored the global drug gap in a 2000 article in Science, emphasizing disparities in access to essential medications. 12. The United Nations Development Programme compiled a compendium of basic specifications for emergency relief items in 1999, offering a resource for disaster response. 13. The WHO published guidelines in 1998 for the development and operation of district health facilities, focusing on improving healthcare delivery in resource-limited settings. 14. Krantz BE discussed the international Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS) program in Trauma Quarterly in 1999, highlighting its global impact on trauma care. 15. Wilkinson DA and Skinner MW authored a primary trauma care manual in 2000, designed for trauma management in district and remote locations. 16. Maier RV and Rhodes M contributed to a guide on trauma performance improvement in the book Injury Control: A Guide to Research and Program Evaluation, published by Cambridge University Press in 2001. 17. Shackford SR et al. examined the role of the Medical Audit Committee in ensuring quality within trauma systems, as reported in the Journal of Trauma in 1987. 18. Pathak L et al. analyzed process indicators for safe motherhood programs using hospital data from Nepal, as reported in Tropical Medicine and International Health in 2000. 22. Bhatt R emphasized the role of medical audits in ensuring professional responsibility in maternity care, as published in the International Journal of Gynecology & Obstetrics in 1989. 23. Ifenne D et al. described efforts to improve the quality of obstetric care at a teaching hospital in Zaria, Nigeria, as reported in the International Journal of Gynecology & Obstetrics in 1997. 24. Ndiaye A et al. analyzed mortality caused by traffic accidents at a trauma and orthopedics center in Senegal over a two-year period, as reported in a French-language study. 40. Ozguc H et al. evaluated the outcomes of major trauma cases in a Turkish university hospital, assessing the impact of an integrated approach, as published in the European Journal of Emergency Medicine in 2000. 41. Mitchell FT, Thal E, and Wolferth C analyzed unsuccessful verification reviews under the American College of Surgeons Verification/Consultation Program, as reported in the Journal of Trauma in 1994. 42. Mock C et al. described improvements in prehospital trauma care in an African country lacking formal emergency medical services, as published in the Journal of Trauma in 2002. 43. Forjuoh S et al. highlighted the need to strengthen trauma care practices in Ghana, particularly in the transport of injured patients to hospitals, as reported in Pre-hospital Immediate Care in 1999.
